source: Team mapping NETIQ_RAN_MW_FTTH_Wireline_Mappings (23 Nov 2026); report sources, view base tables and query rules from the updated NETIQ Java code (received 23 Nov 2026, last commit 20 Nov 2026)

sql_rules.why: Leave out removed rows with STATUS IS NULL OR STATUS <> 'DELETE', the same filter the NETIQ screens use. Do not rely on IS_ACTIVE = 1 alone: the code saves new MW links, cabinets and IP rows with IS_ACTIVE = 0, and BOARD_MW_DATA has no IS_ACTIVE column.
Use parent.ID = child.<link column> from the Relationships sheet. Names and text IDs repeat, so joining on them can multiply rows.
sql_rules.example: JOIN NODE_DATA n ON n.ID = c.ENODEB_CELL

sql_rules.rule: Link columns are named after the parent
sql_rules.why: NODE_DATA, BOARD_DATA, SITE_FOR_NODE, ENODEB_CELL and similar columns hold the parent's ID, not a name.
sql_rules.example: JOIN SITE_DATA s ON s.ID = n.SITE_FOR_NODE

sql_rules.rule: Import run is not the 'current' flag
sql_rules.why: VERSION_ID points to the import run (CIRCLE_DATA_VERSION). Use it to show when data was loaded, not to filter current rows.
sql_rules.example: JOIN CIRCLE_DATA_VERSION v ON v.ID = n.VERSION_ID

sql_rules.why: SITE_DATA keeps one row per site per NMS, so the same SITE_ID can appear more than once.

sql_rules.rule: A node is CIRCLE + NODE_ID + NODE_TYPE
sql_rules.why: NODE_DATA holds SRANBS, ENODEB, GNODEB, BTS and GHOST rows. Node IDs are unique only within a circle.
Data tables use CIRCLE; CIRCLE_DATA_VERSION and summary views use CIRCLE_ID; MIDS tables use 3-letter codes (convert with CIRCLE_MAP).

Every query must be limited to the user's circles. NETIQ takes them from the login response (circleList). ALL, PAN INDIA or an empty list means all circles, the same as NETIQ (confirmed by the team); if NETIQ changes this rule, follow it. Circle names are turned into 2-letter codes first (see Circles).
NETIQ's own views compare names and settings with UPPER(TRIM(...)).
When a NETIQ report covers the question, read its view so the numbers match the screen.
Where the team mapping and the deployed database spell a column differently, use the database name (see Open Questions).
NETIQ counts nodes by NODE_TYPE. For 2G / 4G / 5G counts use SUPPORTED_TECHNOLOGY: a node that supports 2G/4G/5G is counted under each one, and the total is the number of distinct nodes.

sql_rules.rule: Link MW links to MW nodes on NODE1_ID / NODE2_ID
sql_rules.why: NODE1_DATA and NODE2_DATA are mostly empty because the import builds link and node keys differently. Join on the node ID in the same circle and keep one row per node.
sql_rules.example: JOIN NODE_MW_DATA m ON m.NODE_ID = l.NODE1_ID AND m.CIRCLE = l.CIRCLE

sql_rules.why: Wireline rows carry no real circle. Where SITE_ID ends with _<circle code> (for example ..._MH), use that code.

sql_rules.rule: Never use system objects or procedures
sql_rules.why: Only objects marked Allow. Never run procedures or functions.

duplicate_rules.rule: Same node ID within the same circle, vendor, ID source and BTS/non-BTS group; also same node name, and same ID + name.
Same cell ID + cell name within circle and vendor; also ID only and name only.
Same cleaned cell ID + cleaned cell name within the circle (vendor not used); also ID only and name only.
Same node ID + node name + node type (trimmed, upper case) within circle and vendor; also node ID only across NMS sources.
Same board serial number + board name more than once (latest per node kept).
Same serial number on more than one MW board.
Same IP address on more than one node within a circle.

questions_and_answers.question: What do the columns and code values mean?
questions_and_answers.answer: The team's descriptions only repeat the column name. Screen labels are shown for 1,026 columns (from the NETIQ reports). Code values from the NETIQ code: STATUS is NEW, UPDATE or DELETE; NODE_TYPE is SRANBS, ENODEB, GNODEB, BTS or GHOST.
questions_and_answers.why: The SQL Agent needs meanings to pick the right column.

questions_and_answers.question: Which tables is each view built from?
questions_and_answers.answer: Read from the NETIQ SQL scripts and code for 75 of 77 views (see 'Built from' in the Tables and views sheet). No SQL exists anywhere for: CELL_RU_MAPPING_VALIDATION_VIEW, STABLE_DETAIL_VIEW.
questions_and_answers.why: Needed to trace a report number back to its tables.

questions_and_answers.question: Do STABLE_DETAIL_VIEW and CELL_RU_MAPPING_VALIDATION_VIEW exist on production?
questions_and_answers.answer: The Change Details report and the Cell-RU mapping audit read them, but there is no SQL for them in the NETIQ code and they are not in our database copy.
questions_and_answers.why: Those two reports may not work without them.

questions_and_answers.question: The updated code has 2 views that are not in the mapping (VW_ERROR_REPORT_WITHOUT_SUGGESTION, VW_ERROR_REPORT_WITH_SUGGESTION).
questions_and_answers.answer: They feed the two new Error Reports. Their SQL is in the NETIQ code, so we can add them ourselves.
questions_and_answers.why: The SQL Agent can only use objects it knows.

questions_and_answers.question: 9 objects are in the mapping but not in our database copy.
questions_and_answers.answer: Most are created by newer NETIQ scripts that have not been run on our copy. VW_PLANNED_VS_CONFIGURED_TRLINK appears only in old scripts; the reports use VW_PLAN_VS_CONFIG_TRLINK.
questions_and_answers.why: The SQL Agent must not use objects that do not exist.

questions_and_answers.question: 10 objects are in our database copy but not in the mapping.
questions_and_answers.answer: None of them is used by the NETIQ code. They are leftovers, and the SQL Agent will ignore them.
questions_and_answers.why: Keeps the SQL Agent away from old objects.

questions_and_answers.question: 23 objects spell some column names differently from the database.
questions_and_answers.answer: The NETIQ code's naming rule gives the database spelling (for example MISSINGERFCN, NODE_ID). SQL uses the database spelling.
questions_and_answers.why: SQL fails if a column name is wrong.

questions_and_answers.question: 5 objects have a different type (view or materialized view), and many view columns have no data type.
questions_and_answers.answer: Not needed for now: the SQL Agent reads views and materialized views the same way. Refresh timing of materialized views is to be checked with the DBA.
questions_and_answers.why: Affects how fresh the numbers are.

questions_and_answers.question: Are any columns personal data?
questions_and_answers.answer: No column is marked as personal data, and no column name looks like a password, phone number or e-mail.
questions_and_answers.why: Decides what the chatbot may show.

questions_and_answers.question: How are the FTTH tables, and the Wireline tables, linked to each other?
questions_and_answers.answer: The NETIQ code never joins them, and our database copy has no FTTH or Wireline data to test. Likely links by column name: link NODE_A_ID / NODE_B_ID and port or hardware NODE_ID point to the node's NE_ID.
questions_and_answers.why: FTTH and Wireline questions cannot join tables until this is known.

questions_and_answers.question: Is IS_ACTIVE = 1 the right way to find current rows?
questions_and_answers.answer: No. Use STATUS <> 'DELETE', the same filter the NETIQ screens use. The import saves new MW links, cabinets and IP rows with IS_ACTIVE = 0 (an import issue), and BOARD_MW_DATA has no IS_ACTIVE column.
questions_and_answers.why: Wrong filter hides new records.

questions_and_answers.question: Why are NODE1_DATA / NODE2_DATA mostly empty on MW links?
questions_and_answers.answer: The import builds the link's node key differently from the node's own key, so most never match. Join on NODE1_ID / NODE2_ID = NODE_ID in the same circle instead.
questions_and_answers.why: Needed to join MW links to their nodes.

questions_and_answers.question: Where does the circle come from for FTTH and Wireline?
questions_and_answers.answer: They are loaded as fixed circles (FTTH, WIRELINE). For Wireline, the circle can be read from the end of SITE_ID (for example ..._MH) where it is present.
questions_and_answers.why: Circle filters must work on every area.

questions_and_answers.question: Do these fields hold the same ID: neId / nodeId, btsId / nodeId, hopId / linkId?
questions_and_answers.answer: btsId and nodeId are different (2G cells link to the node by BTS_ID). hopId is the planned hop; the live link is in LIVE_LINK_ID. neId / nodeId in Wireline look the same but are part of the FTTH/Wireline question.
questions_and_answers.why: Wrong ID gives wrong joins.

questions_and_answers.question: Which filters does each report API support?
questions_and_answers.answer: Circle, vendor, type, node type, technology, search, sorting, paging, and column filters with 20 operators (equals, contains, between, in and so on). Unknown filter names are ignored without an error.
questions_and_answers.why: The chatbot must send filters the API understands.

questions_and_answers.question: Where do the dashboard numbers come from?
questions_and_answers.answer: They are counted live from SITE_VIEW, NODE_VIEW, CELL_INVENTORY_VIEW and BOARD_VIEW, not from INVENTORY_METRICS.
questions_and_answers.why: Chatbot numbers should match the dashboard.

questions_and_answers.question: How should sites be counted?
questions_and_answers.answer: One row per SITE_ID (the latest), across circles. Use COUNT(DISTINCT SITE_ID).
questions_and_answers.why: Avoids counting a site twice.

questions_and_answers.question: How should nodes be counted per technology?
questions_and_answers.answer: NETIQ counts by node type. For technology, use SUPPORTED_TECHNOLOGY and count a node under each technology it supports (see SQL rules).
questions_and_answers.why: An SRAN node can serve 2G, 4G and 5G.

questions_and_answers.question: Should the chatbot show removed records?
questions_and_answers.answer: Yes. NETIQ already has a Deleted Reports page, so the chatbot can answer questions like 'what was removed last week'.
questions_and_answers.why: Users ask about changes.

questions_and_answers.question: Which read-only database user will the SQL Agent use?
questions_and_answers.answer: NETIQ_DEV (confirmed by the team). It must only read the allowed tables and views; the SQL Agent also checks every query before it runs.
questions_and_answers.why: The SQL Agent must only read allowed tables.

questions_and_answers.question: Where do each user's allowed circles come from?
questions_and_answers.answer: From the NETIQ login: it returns the user's circle list. ALL or PAN INDIA means all circles. Confirmed by the team: the chatbot follows NETIQ, so a user with no circles assigned sees all circles; if NETIQ changes this rule, the chatbot must follow it.
questions_and_answers.why: Every query must be limited to the user's circles.
